cards.text: Jeremiah, a prophet to Judah, has just heard the LORD say Jerusalem will become a heap of rubble. Now a question goes out: who is wise enough to understand this? Why is the land destroyed and scorched like a desert, so no one can pass through it?

cards.question: Who answers the question of why the land is destroyed?
The LORD says the land is ruined because the people have forsaken His ___ and have not obeyed His voice.

cards.text: Instead, the LORD says, they followed the stubbornness of their hearts. Believe me, I know stubborn: I once told a whole kitchen my cookies weren't burnt while the smoke alarm was singing BACKUP.

cards.question: Following their stubborn hearts, who did the people go after?
The LORD says the people came up with chasing the Baals all on their own, with nobody teaching them.

cards.text: So the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says He will feed this people wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink. That's not a menu, friend. That's a WARNING.

cards.question: After the wormwood and the poisoned water, where does the LORD say He will scatter the people?

answers.text: Among nations they have never known

cards.text: And He will send a sword after them until He has finished them off. This is where the stubborn road ends.

Then the LORD of Hosts says to take note and summon the wailing women, and send for the most skillful among them. Skilled mourners, friend. And here I am, the guy who cried over one cracked cookie for FREE.

cards.question: The LORD wants the wailing women to come quickly and take up a ___ over the people.

cards.text: Then the sound of wailing is heard from Zion: 'How devastated we are! How great is our shame!'

cards.question: The people in Zion cry that they have abandoned the land because their dwellings have been torn down.

cards.text: Now the women are told to open their ears to the word of the LORD. Then they're to teach their daughters to wail, and teach one another to lament.

cards.question: Here's the reason for all the wailing. Something has climbed in through the windows and entered the fortresses. What is it?

cards.text: Death has come in to cut off the children from the streets and the young men from the town squares.
Then comes the word of the LORD: the corpses of men will fall like dung on the open field, like newly cut grain behind the reaper.

cards.question: The LORD says someone will come along behind and gather up the fallen.

cards.text: Then the LORD says not to let the wise man boast in his wisdom, or the strong man in his strength. Friend, I used to brag about my sharp edges on that kitchen counter, and those edges got me YEARS in the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: There's a third man on the list. The LORD says the wealthy man shouldn't boast in his ___.
So if someone is going to boast, what does the LORD say to boast in?

answers.text: That he understands and knows the LORD
That he keeps every rule perfectly
That he gives more than his neighbors

cards.text: And the One they'd know is the LORD, who exercises loving devotion, justice and righteousness on the earth. Now THAT'S worth bragging about, and way better than sharp edges.

cards.question: The LORD says loving devotion, justice and righteousness are things He puts up with but doesn't delight in.

cards.text: Then the LORD says, 'Behold, the days are coming,' when He will punish all who are circumcised only in the flesh.

cards.question: Judah is on the LORD's list right alongside Egypt, Edom, Ammon and Moab.

cards.text: So are all the inhabitants of the desert who clip the hair of their temples. And the LORD says all these nations are uncircumcised.

cards.question: And the whole house of Israel? The LORD says they are uncircumcised in ___.

findings.problem: The opening card says Jeremiah has just heard the LORD say Jerusalem will become a heap of rubble. That fact comes from Jeremiah 9:11, which is outside the passage. The card gives no reference for it and cites only Jeremiah 9:12.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke adds a new moment to the Millers' kitchen backstory. In that story, Papa Dorin was a stamper and Mother Miller did the baking, but here he insists that his own cookies weren't burnt. 'The smoke alarm was singing BACKUP' also doesn't land right away. A stranger would likely say 'huh?' at backup singers.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: Card 10 says to summon the wailing women and calls them skilled mourners. That rules out 'celebration' and 'blessing' as wrong answers before the question is asked.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke contradicts Papa Dorin's backstory. It says he bragged about his sharp edges and that those edges got him years in the junk drawer. In the backstory, he went into the drawer because his edges had worn soft and his stamps came out blurry, and nothing says he bragged.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: 'Way better than sharp edges' is a callback to the stop 2 card 1 joke. That joke contradicts the backstory, so the callback carries the same false version of his story.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The statement says 'the LORD's list' without saying what the list is. The context that it lists people the LORD will punish for being circumcised only in the flesh is on card 6, which is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
